mainTopic: Can a יבם nullify the נדרים of a שומרת יבם (a widow waiting for him to do יבום)?
overview: This amud deals with a widow whose husband died without children. She is now a שומרת יבם, waiting for his brother to do יבום or חליצה. The משנה asks whether that brother, the יבם, can cancel her vows the way a husband can. רבי אליעזר says yes, and argues it with a קל וחומר. רבי יהושע says yes only when there is one יבם. רבי עקיבא says never, because a יבמה is not fully bound to the יבם the way an ארוסה is bound to her husband. The גמרא explains רבי עקיבא and רבי יהושע through the question of זיקה. It then asks how רבי אליעזר can allow cancellation when there are several brothers and no ברירה. רבי אמי answers that one brother already did מאמר, and רבי אליעזר holds like בית שמאי that מאמר is a full קנין. The גמרא challenges this from רבי אלעזר, who holds that for בית שמאי מאמר only pushes away the צרה. It answers that the יבם was also ordered by בית דין to support her, and a woman vows with her husband's consent in mind.

steps.title: Three opinions on a יבם cancelling the vows of a שומרת יבם
steps.stepSummary: The משנה presents the case of a שומרת יבם and gives three opinions on whether the יבם can cancel her vows.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: A widow waiting for יבום, whether there is one brother or two: רבי אליעזר says the יבם can cancel her vows. רבי יהושע says he can if there is one brother, but not if there are two. רבי עקיבא says he cannot, whether there is one brother or two.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה lays out the case and three different opinions about whether a יבם can cancel the vows of the widow waiting for him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אליעזר treats the יבם like a husband in every case. רבי יהושע says that depends on whether she is tied to one specific brother or shared between several. רבי עקיבא says the יבם never has this power.

keyTerms.meaning: Short for מַתְנִיתִין, 'our משנה'; marks the start of a משנה
A widow 'waiting for her יבם', meaning her late husband's brother
The brother(s) of the man who died without children
He can cancel (her vows); from the word הֲפָרָה

steps.whyThisMatters: The rest of this section of the משנה is a debate explaining the reasons behind these three opinions.

phrases.english: MISHNA: A woman waiting for her yavam,
phrases.notes: This is a widow whose husband died with no children, so she is waiting for his brother to do יבום or חליצה.

phrases.english: whether she is waiting for one yavam,
or for two yevamin.
Rabbi Eliezer says: He can nullify her vows.
Rabbi Yehoshua says: If she is waiting for one, he can,
but not if she is waiting for two.
Rabbi Akiva says:
Not for one and not for two.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְנִי׳ שׁוֹמֶרֶת יָבָם, בֵּין לְיָבָם אֶחָד, בֵּין לִשְׁנֵי יְבָמִין
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי אליעזר: the יבם can always cancel her vows. רבי יהושע: only when there is one יבם. רבי עקיבא: never.

steps.title: רבי אליעזר's קל וחומר
steps.stepSummary: רבי אליעזר argues that if a husband can cancel the vows of a woman he acquired himself, then surely a יבם can cancel the vows of a woman Heaven gave him.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אליעזר said: A man can cancel the vows of a woman he acquired on his own. Then a woman that Heaven handed to him should surely be included!
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אליעזר gives a reason for his opinion. He uses a קל וחומר, which is a 'how much more so' argument.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The weaker case is a wife the man acquired by his own act, and there he can cancel her vows. The stronger case is a יבמה, whom the Torah itself linked to him. So he should be able to cancel her vows too.

keyTerms.meaning: 'If even…': the opening words of a קל וחומר argument
He acquired for himself, through his own act of קידושין
Heaven acquired her for him, meaning the Torah's יבום bond
'Isn't it logical?': the closing words of a קל וחומר

phrases.english: Rabbi Eliezer said:

phrases.aramaic: מָה אִם אִשָּׁה שֶׁקָּנָה הוּא לְעַצְמוֹ —
phrases.english: If a woman whom he acquired for himself
is one whose vows he can nullify,
then a woman acquired for him from Heaven,
phrases.notes: He means the יבמה. The Torah ties her to the brother without any act on his part.

phrases.english: isn't it logical that he should nullify her vows?

steps.triggerLanguage: מָה אִם אִשָּׁה שֶׁקָּנָה הוּא לְעַצְמוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the reasoning for רבי אליעזר's opinion in step 1.
steps.raayaObject: רבי אליעזר's ruling that a יבם can cancel a שומרת יבם's vows.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A קל וחומר from a woman a man acquires himself, whose vows he can cancel.

steps.title: רבי עקיבא: others also have a share in a יבמה
steps.stepSummary: רבי עקיבא rejects the קל וחומר. A wife he acquired belongs to him alone, but a יבמה is also tied to the other brothers.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי עקיבא said to him: No! A woman he acquired himself is different, because no one else has any claim on her. Can you say the same about a woman Heaven gave him, when other people do have a claim on her?
steps.whatsHappening: רבי עקיבא breaks רבי אליעזר's argument by pointing to a way the 'weaker' case is actually stronger.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A wife a man acquired is his alone. A יבמה is linked to every surviving brother, so no single brother has full authority over her. Because of this difference, the קל וחומר falls apart.

keyTerms.meaning: 'No, if you said…': the standard way to reject a קל וחומר
'Will you say…?' A challenge asking whether the comparison really holds
A claim, or authority over someone

phrases.english: Rabbi Akiva said to him: No,

phrases.aramaic: אִם אָמַרְתָּ בְּאִשָּׁה שֶׁקָּנָה הוּא לְעַצְמוֹ —
phrases.english: if you said this about a woman he acquired for himself
over whom others have no authority,

phrases.aramaic: תֹּאמַר בְּאִשָּׁה שֶׁהִקְנוּ לוֹ מִן הַשָּׁמַיִם,
phrases.english: will you say it about a woman acquired for him from Heaven,
over whom others have authority?!
phrases.notes: The 'others' are the other brothers. Any one of them could do the יבום.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לוֹ רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא: לֹא, אִם אָמַרְתָּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the קל וחומר from step 2.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The whole קל וחומר, though the reason he gives fits best when there are several brothers.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: A wife he acquired belongs only to him, while other brothers also have a share in a יבמה.

steps.title: רבי יהושע: what about only one יבם?
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהושע points out that רבי עקיבא's argument only works when there are two brothers, and asks how he answers the case of one.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהושע said to him: עקיבא, your words work when there are two יבמין. But what is your answer when there is only one יבם?
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יהושע challenges רבי עקיבא. His reason ('others have a share') says nothing when there is only one brother.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When there is only one יבם, nobody else has any claim on her, so רבי עקיבא's reason disappears. This is exactly why רבי יהושע holds that a single יבם can cancel her vows.

keyTerms.meaning: 'What do you answer?' A demand to defend a position
Your words, your argument

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehoshua said to him: Akiva,
your words apply to two yevamin,

phrases.aramaic: מָה אַתָּה מֵשִׁיב עַל יָבָם אֶחָד?
phrases.english: but what do you reply about one yavam?

steps.triggerLanguage: מָה אַתָּה מֵשִׁיב עַל יָבָם אֶחָד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the reason רבי עקיבא gave in step 3.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי עקיבא's rejection in step 3, and his ruling that even one יבם cannot cancel vows.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The 'others have a share' reason does not exist when there is only one brother, so the קל וחומר should still work in that case.

steps.title: רבי עקיבא: a יבמה is not a complete wife
steps.stepSummary: רבי עקיבא answers with a new reason: a יבמה is not fully bound to the יבם the way an ארוסה is bound to her husband.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: A יבמה is not fully the יבם's in the way that an ארוסה is fully her husband's.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי עקיבא answers רבי יהושע with a deeper reason that applies even when there is only one יבם.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The weak point is no longer the other brothers. The bond itself is weaker. An ארוסה is fully bound to her husband through קידושין, but a יבמה is only waiting to be married, so even a single יבם lacks a husband's power to cancel vows.

keyTerms.meaning: The widow who is tied to her late husband's brother
Complete, fully belonging
A woman after קידושין (betrothal) but before נישואין

steps.whatToRemember: רבי אליעזר: a יבם is like a husband because of the קל וחומר. רבי יהושע: it depends on whether others share in her. רבי עקיבא: a יבמה is never fully his, so he cannot cancel her vows.
steps.confusionAlert: רבי עקיבא's final reason is not about the other brothers. It is about the יבום bond itself being incomplete, and that is why it covers the case of one יבם too.

phrases.english: He said to him:
A yevama is not fully belonging to the yavam
in the way that a betrothed woman fully belongs to her husband.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רבי יהושע's challenge from step 4.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי עקיבא's only reason was that other brothers share in her, which fails when there is one יבם.
steps.terutzMaskana: The יבום bond itself is incomplete compared to אירוסין, so no יבם, not even a single one, can cancel her vows.

steps.title: Explaining the opinions, and asking for רבי אליעזר's reason
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains רבי עקיבא and רבי יהושע using זיקה, then asks what רבי אליעזר's reason could be.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: רבי עקיבא makes sense: he holds there is no זיקה. רבי יהושע also makes sense: he holds there is זיקה. But what is רבי אליעזר's reason? Even if there is זיקה, there is no ברירה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא sorts the opinions of the משנה. Two are easy to explain, but רבי אליעזר's view seems hard to understand, so the גמרא asks for his reason.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If there is no זיקה, the יבמה is not his wife at all, so he cannot cancel her vows. That is רבי עקיבא. If there is זיקה, then with one brother she is like his wife. That is רבי יהושע. But רבי אליעזר lets the יבם cancel even when there are several brothers. Since we cannot say looking back which brother she was really tied to (no ברירה), how can any one of them cancel her vows?

keyTerms.meaning: The Talmud's discussion of the משנה
It makes sense / It is understandable (sets up a contrast with a harder case)
The bond that ties a יבמה to her יבם before יבום
Clarifying something afterward, as if it was already decided from the start

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think רבי אליעזר rejects זיקה. The question is that even with זיקה, there is no ברירה to say which brother she belongs to.

phrases.english: GEMARA: It makes sense regarding Rabbi Akiva:
he holds there is no levirate bond,
and Rabbi Yehoshua holds there is a levirate bond.
But Rabbi Eliezer, what is his reason?
Even if there is a bond, there is no retroactive designation.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: The גמרא begins analyzing the משנה's three opinions.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What logic lets רבי אליעזר allow a יבם to cancel vows even when there are several brothers and no ברירה?

steps.title: The case is where one brother already did מאמר
steps.stepSummary: רבי אמי says the case is where one brother did מאמר, and רבי אליעזר follows בית שמאי that מאמר is a full קנין.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אמי said: The case is where he did מאמר with her. רבי אליעזר holds like בית שמאי, who say that מאמר makes a full קנין.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אמי answers the question by narrowing the case. The משנה is talking about a brother who already did מאמר with her.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once a specific brother does מאמר, the problem of 'which brother?' goes away. According to בית שמאי, מאמר fully acquires her, the same as a regular אירוסין. So that brother can cancel her vows, the same way an ארוס can.

keyTerms.meaning: A betrothal-like act a יבם does to a יבמה before יבום
The school of שמאי
A full, complete acquisition

phrases.english: Rabbi Ami said:
It is a case where he performed levirate betrothal with her.

phrases.aramaic: וְרַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר סָבַר לַהּ כְּבֵית שַׁמַּאי,
phrases.english: And Rabbi Eliezer holds like Beit Shammai,
who say: Levirate betrothal effects a full acquisition.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי אַמֵּי: כְּגוֹן שֶׁעָשָׂה בָּהּ מַאֲמָר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question about רבי אליעזר's reason.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The case is after מאמר, and רבי אליעזר holds like בית שמאי that מאמר is a full קנין.

steps.title: How רבי יהושע and רבי עקיבא fit into רבי אמי's explanation
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהושע limits the power of מאמר to a case with one יבם, and רבי עקיבא holds there is no זיקה at all.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהושע would tell you: That rule only applies to one יבם, not to two יבמין. Is there any kind of betrothal where his brother can come and forbid her to him through ביאה or a גט, and yet he can still cancel her vows? And רבי עקיבא holds there is no זיקה.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אמי continues and explains the other two opinions in the משנה, now that the case is after מאמר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהושע argues that when there are two brothers, מאמר cannot be a full קנין. The other brother can still do יבום or give a גט and take her away. A betrothal that someone else can undo is too weak to give the power to cancel vows. רבי עקיבא goes further and says that without זיקה, there is no bond at all before יבום.

keyTerms.meaning: These words apply only... (limits a rule)
Intercourse; here, doing יבום
A bill of divorce (גט)
Cancels a vow

steps.whatToRemember: According to רבי אמי: רבי אליעזר holds מאמר is always a full קנין. רבי יהושע says it is a full קנין only with one יבם. רבי עקיבא says there is no זיקה at all.

phrases.english: And Rabbi Yehoshua would say to you:
That applies only with one yavam,
but with two yevamin, it does not.
Is there anything
where, when his brother comes,
he can forbid her to him through intercourse,
phrases.notes: The other brother does יבום with her himself, so she is now off-limits to the one who did מאמר.

phrases.english: or through a bill of divorce, and yet he can nullify her vows?
And Rabbi Akiva holds: there is no levirate bond.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ אוֹמֵר לְךָ: הָנֵי מִילֵּי בְּחַד יָבָם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes רבי אמי's explanation by fitting the remaining two opinions into his case.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רבי יהושע: מאמר is a full קנין only with one יבם, because a second brother can undo it. רבי עקיבא: there is no זיקה.

steps.title: Challenge from רבי אלעזר's view of בית שמאי
steps.stepSummary: According to רבי אלעזר, בית שמאי hold that מאמר only pushes away the צרה, so רבי אמי's explanation seems to fall apart.
steps.simpleTranslation: And according to רבי אלעזר, who said that for בית שמאי, מאמר does not acquire her except to push away the צרה, what can be said?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רבי אמי's answer. Another אמורא understands בית שמאי's view of מאמר differently.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אמי's answer depends on בית שמאי holding that מאמר is a full קנין. But רבי אלעזר says that for בית שמאי, מאמר only pushes away the צרה. If that is right, מאמר is not a real betrothal, and it is unclear how רבי אליעזר could let the יבם cancel vows.

keyTerms.meaning: A co-wife; here, the other widow of the dead brother
To push away
What is there to say? It asks how a position can still be defended. The next step answers it.

phrases.english: And according to Rabbi Elazar, who said:
phrases.notes: Some versions say אליעזר, in the round brackets. The right name is אלעזר, in the square brackets: the later אמורא, not the תנא from the משנה.

phrases.english: Levirate betrothal, according to Beit Shammai, does not acquire
except to push away the rival wife.
What can be said?

steps.triggerLanguage: וּלְרַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר, דְּאָמַר: מַאֲמָר לְבֵית שַׁמַּאי אֵין קוֹנֶה אֶלָּא לִדְחוֹת בַּצָּרָה. מַאי אִיכָּא לְמֵימַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the foundation of רבי אמי's answer in step 7.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי אמי's claim that רבי אליעזר follows בית שמאי, for whom מאמר is a full קנין.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי אלעזר says בית שמאי give מאמר only the limited power to push away the צרה, not full betrothal. So the explanation of רבי אליעזר has no basis.

steps.title: The case is where the court obligated the יבם to support her
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא saves רבי אמי's explanation. It sets the case where the יבם was ordered by בית דין to provide her מזונות. Since a woman vows on her husband's consent, a יבם who supports her can annul her vows.
steps.simpleTranslation: Here we are talking about a case where the יבם stood trial in court and was obligated to provide her food and support. This follows רב פנחס in the name of רבא, who said: any woman who makes a vow makes it with her husband's consent in mind.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the קשיא by saying the משנה's case is narrower. The יבם was ordered by the court to support the יבמה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The challenge was that מאמר alone (per רבי אלעזר's version of בית שמאי) is too weak to make her his wife for annulling vows. The answer adds a second factor: he is now legally supporting her. According to רבי אמי's approach, רבי אליעזר holds that once he supports her, her vows are made 'on his consent,' so he can annul them, using the rule of רב פנחס.

keyTerms.meaning: "Here, what are we dealing with?" The גמרא uses this phrase to narrow a source to a specific case.
He stood in judgment, meaning he was brought to court.
Food and financial support owed to a woman.
With her husband's consent in mind, so her vow depends on his approval.
A woman who makes a vow.

steps.whatToRemember: The יבם's power to annul here does not come from מאמר alone. It comes from מאמר plus a court order to support her, together with the rule that a woman vows on her husband's consent.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not think the גמרא is now saying מאמר is a full קנין. It accepts רבי אלעזר's view that it is not, and finds a different basis: the support obligation.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that even if מאמר alone is weak, adding a court-ordered duty to support her can be enough to give the יבם power over her vows.

phrases.english: Here, what are we dealing with?
Such as where he stood in judgment,
phrases.notes: "He" is the יבם. She took him to court demanding that he marry her.

phrases.english: and he was obligated to provide her sustenance.
And this is in line with Rav Pinchas in the name of Rava:
who said: Any woman who vows,
she vows on her husband's consent.
phrases.notes: Since the יבם now supports her, he counts as the 'husband' whose consent her vows depend on.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 9 by narrowing the case and bringing a supporting principle.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Narrowing the case (אוקימתא) plus an outside principle (רב פנחס in the name of רבא).
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since מאמר only pushes away the צרה, the יבם should have no power to annul her vows, so רבי אמי's explanation falls apart.
steps.terutzMaskana: The case is where the court obligated him to support her. A woman vows on the consent of the one who supports her as husband, so he can annul.
